small_guidance:
- Add a swizzle/group ordering (group along M) and larger N tiles (e.g. BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_K=64) since OC=64 makes M tiny — most parallelism must come from N=64*254*254≈4.1M; ensure grid prioritizes pid_n for L2 reuse of weights.
- Since IC=64 and KH=KW=3, K_total=576 — try BLOCK_K=64 or 96 with num_stages=4 and num_warps=8 to better pipeline the small K loop; also unroll the KH/KW loops explicitly (nested for over kh,kw with BLOCK_K over IC only) so kh/kw become constexpr and index math is hoisted.
- Drop the per-iteration recomputation of `ic_k/kh_k/kw_k` by restructuring to outer kh,kw loops (constexpr) and inner IC tile loop — saves integer divs in the hot K-loop.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as channels-last (NHWC) implicit GEMM: pack x to NHWC once (cheap, one-time-ish per call but amortized), so the GEMM-K dimension (IC) is contiguous and loads coalesce without gather strides; weights laid out as [KH,KW,IC,OC] enable plain matmul tiles.
- Replace the single fused K loop with explicit nested loops over (kh, kw) as constexpr and an inner IC reduction with BLOCK_K=IC (=64) — eliminates divisions in index math and lets Triton emit clean ldmatrix patterns; the spatial tile becomes a 2D (BH, BW) block instead of flat N to improve halo reuse across the kh,kw loops.
- Consider a persistent-kernel scheme: each program iterates over multiple output tiles to amortize weight loads (OC=64 is tiny so weights fit in SMEM/regs across the whole K dimension — load weights once per program and stream through many spatial tiles).
